candidates.title: Engagement Estimation in Human-Robot and Human-Human Interactions across Domain, Age and Culture: MultiMediate '26 Challenge
candidates.finding: The authors report a cross-domain engagement-estimation benchmark with adult conversations and PInSoRo child-child/child-robot play. Continuous engagement and categorical social/task engagement are evaluated with distinct metrics (CCC and Cohen's kappa). Validation/test sessions have at least two raters; test frames for each subtask are scored only where all annotators agree. PInSoRo source videos and transcripts are withheld for privacy; derived features are provided. arXiv records v1 submitted 2026-08-25; the associated ACM Multimedia conference was November 10-14, 2026, not a new November 16 paper publication.
candidates.hilo_adaptation: Propose an advisory, non-ranking human-robot interaction evidence card: keep inter-rater agreement and disagreement, task-vs-social engagement, domain and demographic distribution, and source/privacy limitations visible. Never equate short-term engagement with voluntary long-term keep/rejection votes, never extrapolate 10,000 real robot hours, never ingest minors' video/transcripts or feature vectors without rights, consent, child-data safeguards and human review. Preserve sealed holdouts, non-compensatory safety, frozen WANTED scoring and independent source classes.
